summary.text: Raúl Torrez is the Democratic incumbent Attorney General of New Mexico, seeking a second term after serving as Bernalillo County district attorney and as a federal prosecutor. His office has prioritized child protection, including lawsuits against Meta and Snap, and joined a multistate lawsuit challenging a federal fuel-economy rule.

paragraphs.text: Torrez graduated from Harvard University, where he earned a bachelor's degree in government, and earned a master's degree from the London School of Economics.
He worked for the Cesar Chavez Foundation in Los Angeles before earning his law degree from Stanford Law School in 2005.

Torrez began his legal career in 2005 as an assistant district attorney in Valencia County and the next year joined the New Mexico Attorney General's office; Source NM reports that he began his career litigating child abuse cases.
He served as chief counsel to House Speaker Ben Luján in 2008 and as a White House Fellow in the class of 2009–2010 under President Barack Obama.
He then returned to Albuquerque as a prosecutor in the U.S. Attorney's Office and a senior adviser in the U.S. Department of Justice, and ran a solo law firm.
Torrez won the Democratic nomination for Bernalillo County district attorney in 2016 and the general election without Republican opposition, serving from 2017 to 2023.
In 2022 he defeated State Auditor Brian Colón in the Democratic primary for Attorney General and Republican Jeremy Gay in the general election, 55.3% to 44.6%, and took office in January 2023.
As Attorney General, Torrez has focused on child safety, consumer protection, environmental enforcement and government transparency.
His office's undercover investigations of online child exploitation include Operation MetaPhile and Operation Overwatch.
In August 2026 a court ordered Meta to pay $942 million and overhaul protections for children on Facebook and Instagram in the New Mexico case.
Torrez's wife, Nasha, is an attorney and a dean at the University of New Mexico, and they have two children.
